step: fee-probes (discovery experiments that established the fee/limit model)

cases.probe: key A spend with client-default fee token pathUSD but NO pathUSD limit entry on the key
cases.observed: REJECTED: Account keychain error: SpendingLimitExceeded(SpendingLimitExceeded) during eth_sendRawTransactionSync
cases.classification: estimation/preflight rejection (no receipt, no tx hash)
cases.conclusion: With enforceLimits=true, FEE PAYMENT is itself limit-enforced; a key whose limit set has no entry for the fee token cannot pay fees at all.

cases.probe: same key A spend with explicit feeToken = AlphaUSD (the limit token)
cases.conclusion: Fees paid in the LIMIT TOKEN count against that token limit (561 deducted = 1 transfer + 560 fee).
Root account has no limits; fee model normal (feePayer = sender).

cases.probe: accessKey.updateSpendingLimit adding a pathUSD limit to a key authorized without one
cases.observed: SUCCESS; sets limit AND remaining, but period is 0 (lifetime) - updateSpendingLimit cannot set a period
cases.conclusion: Fee-token limits with recurring periods must be configured AT AUTHORIZATION TIME (the re-authorized keys A-D include pathUSD limits at authorize time).

cases.probe: updateSpendingLimit on an EXPIRED key (old key C)
cases.observed: REVERTED: Account keychain error: KeyExpired(KeyExpired) - preflight
cases.conclusion: Expiry enforcement applies to keychain management calls targeting the key.

finalConfiguration: All subsequent evidence uses keys authorized with DUAL limits: [collection token recurring ceiling, pathUSD fee-token recurring allowance] and scope transfer(collection token) -> treasury only.
